notes:
Summary:
- SMB inbound (self-serve) converting to trial; primary product interest: hosted_api streaming + function/tool-calling for support agent chat flow.
- Main pain: when they enable JSON/structured output mode and stream tokens, their client-side JSON parser frequently throws errors because streams sometimes cut mid-JSON (missing trailing brace/bracket) or model emits small formatting deviations (numbers as strings, trailing commas).
- They are using function-calling schema to enforce structure, but observed that 'name' and 'id' fields occasionally arrive as arrays/strings vs expected primitives -> schema mismatch errors on our side.

Repro notes (from INF-1123 attachments and call):
- Run: hosted_api streaming (chunked) -> client assembles tokens into buffer -> JSON.parse(buffer) -> crash if final chunk truncated. Example transcript shows last chunk dropped by client network retry.
- Function schema: declared 'order_id' integer; model returned '"12345"' or '12345\n' in some runs. SE saw 3/20 runs inconsistent.
- They set temperature=0.7 for more diverse responses (wanted paraphrase), which increased schema drift.

Customer quotes / context:
- CTO (Elena Park): "If we have to patch in post-processing it's OK, but we need clear patterns so retries / fixes don't blow up token costs."
- PM: "Streaming is great for UX but our desktop clients choke when parse errors happen — want a robust approach without rewriting parsers across all clients."

SE suggested immediate mitigations we discussed on call:
- Recommend function-calling structured output (preferred) instead of free-form JSON where possible; it returns single typed arguments instead of open JSON payloads.
- For streaming + JSON assembly: emit a single top-level JSON object and send a final sentinel token (e.g., '\n<END_JSON>') so clients can detect completion rather than relying on connection close.
- Enforce low temperature (0–0.2) for strict schema adherence.
- Add model-side post-processing: run a lightweight schema-fixer step (strip trailing commas, coerce numeric strings) before returning final token stream — propose code snippet in follow-up.
- Suggest retry policy: if parse fails on finalization step, request small deterministic re-run (use same conversation id + top_k=1).

Action items / next steps:
- SE (Rohit) will prepare a short POC repo (node/ts) showing streaming assembly patterns, sentinel usage, and tolerant JSON parser (link to repo stub will be provided).
- AE (Ava) to schedule 30m debug session w/ CTO + eng lead to run live repro and test suggested fixes (target week of 2026-03-22).
- Send best-practices doc: "Streaming + Function-Calling: JSON-mode patterns" + sample SDK snippets.
- Provide a temporary reduced-scope POC token with limited spend so SparkCove can run 100 repeatability tests.

Notes about procurement and ROI:
- SparkCove is price-sensitive but willing to pay for predictable latency; estimate ARR target $10k–$50k if hosted_api proves reliable without heavy engineering overhead.

Open questions we promised to answer:
- Can Redwood provide a recommended default response_format and stop-sentinel for streaming + function-calling? (SE to propose in write-up)
- Any server-side toggles to auto-coerce simple schema mismatches (e.g., numeric strings -> numbers) before final emission? (escalate to infra if needed)

Linked artifacts: INF-1123 (ticket) contains full transcript + sample raw stream; Fireflies ff_20260304_4312 for call audio; initial pricing deck attached in drive/pricing.

Short-term success criteria (customer):
- < 1% parse-failure rate on 500 streaming calls in POC.
- Consistent function-calling argument types across runs (>= 99% pass)
- Predictable token usage for typical 300-token responses (no >20% variance due to retries).
